title: Apple put podcasting inside iTunes.
description:
Apple put podcasting inside iTunes. Odeo was a podcasting company. Its boss, Evan Williams, asked staff for new ideas.

An Odeo engineer who proposed the status idea. Everyone NBC interviewed agreed it began with him.

The pitch: text one number, tell your friends. Noah Glass, Dorsey and contractor Florian Webber presented it as Twttr.

The limit, based on the maximum length of a text message at the time.

just setting up my twttr Dorsey's first message. The public launch followed on 15 July 2006.

Odeo's investors were bought out. Williams said the company was going nowhere. They had put in about 5 million dollars. The price was never reported.

The side project outlived the company.

Sources:
- https://www.nbcnews.com/id/wbna42577600 (read): established that Odeo had a podcasting platform in July 2005; that in fall 2005 Apple announced iTunes with built in podcasting and Evan Williams asked staff for new directions; that Jack Dorsey proposed the status idea, which everyone interviewed agreed on; that in February 2006 Noah Glass, Dorsey and contractor Florian Webber presented it as Twttr, a text to one number broadcast to friends; that a prototype worked in March 2006; and that in September 2006 Williams told investors, who had put in about 5 million dollars, that Odeo was going nowhere and bought their shares back at an unreported price.
- https://www.history.com/this-day-in-history/twitter-launches (read): established that Twttr launched publicly on 15 July 2006 from Odeo; that it used the number 40404; that Dorsey's first message was just setting up my twttr on 21 March; and that the 140 character limit was based on the maximum text message length of the time.
